title: Hosted Interaction Lite PRD — scope re-alignment, acceptance criteria, and launch tasklist
creator: Priya Shah
description: This PRD defines a trimmed 'Lite' bundle of hosted interaction endpoints (generation/chat-completions, embeddings, lightweight rerank) that targets developer adoption for low-latency, low-cost use-cases. The goal is a controlled launch with clear behavioral contracts, deterministic fallback behavior, and a minimal operational surface so we can ship quickly while preserving reliability for higher-tier customers. This ticket captures scope adjustments from stakeholder syncs, explicit acceptance criteria, and a prescriptive launch tasklist (engineering, design, docs, and SRE).
scope_changes: Reduced initial surface to: chat/completions (single-turn), embeddings (dense vectors), and a synchronous top-k rerank API — removed streaming, multimodal, and stateful session features from MVP.
Dropped: fine-grained lane SLAs and tenant burst pool in initial rollout — deferred to Dedicated roadmap (PM-462008).
Added: deterministic fallback rule to a smaller quantized model family when primary model unavailable (see rollout_plan).
Scope change rationale: reduce unknowns for launch to improve latency SLO hit rates and simplify rollout testing matrix.
requirements: API surface: single REST endpoint per capability with identical auth/headers as existing hosted API; support token-based billing and per-request model selection parameter.
Behavioral contracts: for chat/completions, provide stable seeding behavior for identical inputs within a deployment version; document nondeterminism expectations and RNG controls.

Latency and cost targets: median 95th-percentile latency for single-turn completions <= 220ms for small models and <= 420ms for medium models under typical dev load (10rps). Target cost/unit metrics must be documented in console analytics.
Embeddings: 512-d float32 vectors for now; ensure compatibility with similarity pipeline (cosine) and bulk batching with clear per-item timeout semantics.
Rerank: synchronous rerank returns top-k with score breakdown and stable tie-breaking; must support up to k=10 and handle 100 candidate inputs within 350ms P95 for small models.
Operational: rollout must include circuit breaker thresholds and automatic graded fallback to a quantized variant of the same family when tail latency exceeds configured SLO for >2 minutes.
Telemetry: per-route token-level cost, latency histograms by model, error taxonomy (5xx, 4xx, timeout), and distinct metric for fallback activations.
Docs & SDKs: one compact quickstart example per capability (JS + Python), and an OpenAPI spec to power self-serve integration.
acceptance_criteria: Unit and integration tests: >=90% coverage for endpoint validation logic; CI must run performance smoke (local harness) and pass latency gates.
Behavioral tests: deterministic replay harness reproduces 1000 golden prompts with stable top-1 distribution within 2% variance across two sequential deployments of same model version.
Performance SLOs: under synthetic dev load (10rps), P95 latency targets for each capability met in staging for 24h continuous run with <1% error rate.
Fallback correctness: when induced kernel slowdown triggers fallback, 100% of in-flight requests either complete with quantized variant or return a structured degrade response; no silent failures.
Observability: Console shows per-route latency, cost attribution, and histogram-linked request traces. On-call runbook created and validated with a tabletop exercise.
Docs: Quickstart + API reference published in docs site; changelog entry and migration notes for users of older hosted endpoints.
Security: security review completed and KMS integration validated for any customer-supplied artifacts; pen test checklist items closed.
launch_checklist: Engineering: final PR merged for endpoint handlers + rollout policy (GH PR: github.com/redwood-inference/hosted-api/pull/5621).
Performance: run 24h staging perf run and upload report to runtime-perf dashboard (#dash-rt-23).
SRE: create and verify circuit breaker configs, fallback policies, and alerts (PagerDuty runbook created).
Design/UX: inline response examples and error pages reviewed by Design (DES-3344) and copy signed off.
Docs: publish quickstarts (JS/Python), OpenAPI spec, and migration notes; link in console onboarding modal.
Compliance: complete security review and record evidence in GDrive /security/reviews/PM-880882.
Beta customers: enroll 3 pilot teams and perform integration smoke with their SDKs; collect feedback within first 2 weeks.
Incidents: schedule 1 day of on-call overlap post-launch for high-priority handling and log initial issues into tracking board.
Telemetry: ensure per-route cost attribution visible in console and billing reports validated with finance for at least one test org.
Rollout gates: manual canary to 1% traffic for 6 hours, expand to 10% for 12 hours if no exceedances, then 100% in 48 hours.
rollout_plan: Canary stage: deploy to region-us-east-1 with 1% traffic (canary) for 6 hours; monitor latency, error rate, & fallback activations.
Graduated ramp: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% per gate with at least 12h stable window between 10% and 50% transitions unless explicitly approved.
Fallback behavior: if P95 tail latency > configured SLO for >2 consecutive windows (5m windows) trigger automated fallback to quantized variant for affected requests and send alert.
Regional cutover: after global 100% cutover in primary region, begin secondary regions in rolling fashion with 24h separation to validate cross-region config.
Rollback criteria: if fallback activations >5% of requests for 30 minutes or any user-facing 5xx rate >1% sustained, initiate rollback to previous stable deployment and page engineering.
Pilot engagement: maintain a pilot flag for pilot orgs to observe extended telemetry for 14 days before general availability.
tradeoffs: Time-to-market vs features: omitting streaming and session-state reduces developer friction for initial launch but defers important use-cases (conversations, multimodal).

Determinism vs diversity: we emphasize deterministic behavior and seeded replay for the Lite tier which limits sampling-based creativity; this aligns with enterprise reproducibility goals but may disappoint some consumer use-cases.

Fallback complexity: using quantized fallback improves availability and cost but may introduce small distribution shifts—explicitly call this out in docs and provide a deprecation window for deterministic guarantees.
